title: Picsou: Enabling Replicated State Machines to Communicate Efficiently
problem: Replicated state machines (RSMs) in distributed systems cannot communicate effectively; there is no formal framework or efficient protocol for cross-RSM communication, hindering multi-cluster deployments and coordination.
motivation: Efficient RSM communication enables practical multi-cluster systems for disaster recovery, data reconciliation, and distributed applications.
method: PICSOU introduces C3B, a communication method for replicated state machines (systems maintaining identical data copies across many servers) in different data centers. Based on how TCP makes internet connections reliable, C3B keeps bookkeeping overhead constant as systems grow and only retransmits messages that actually failed. It achieves this through QUACKs—quorum acknowledgments where nodes ask a voting majority of other nodes "did you get this message?"—giving precise knowledge of what safely arrived.
key_novelty: C3B, using quorum acknowledgments (a voting mechanism for servers to confirm message arrival), enables replicated state machines to communicate reliably across distant data centers while maintaining strong consistency.
contributions: C3B primitive for replicated state machine communication
QUACK mechanism for precise message delivery tracking
Support for both crash-fault and Byzantine-fault tolerant protocols
24x better performance than prior solutions on microbenchmarks
Practical applications: disaster recovery, data reconciliation
limitations: Scalability to very large clusters and handling of network partitions beyond normal failure assumptions require further study.
